bottom_line: In 45 852 patients with suspected acute MI, allocation to metoprolol versus placebo did not significantly reduce the co-primary composite outcome (OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.90–1.01) or death (OR 0.99, 0.92–1.05) during the scheduled treatment period in hospital.
implications: These results support that, during the scheduled in-hospital treatment period, metoprolol did not produce a statistically significant reduction in the co-primary composite outcome (2166 [9.4%] vs 2261 [9.9%]; OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.90–1.01) or death (1774 [7.7%] vs 1797 [7.8%]; OR 0.99, 0.92–1.05). They also support that metoprolol was associated with fewer reinfarctions (464 [2.0%] vs 568 [2.5%]) and fewer ventricular fibrillation events (581 [2.5%] vs 698 [3.0%]) but more cardiogenic shock (1141 [5.0%] vs 885 [3.9%]) in this setting and timeframe.

major_points.text: Randomised placebo-controlled trial in suspected acute MI, with early intravenous then oral metoprolol versus placebo.
major_points.quote: Early intravenous then oral metoprolol in 45 852 patients with acute myocardial infarction: randomised placebo-controlled trial

major_points.text: Patients were recruited from 1250 hospitals within 24 h of suspected acute MI onset.
major_points.quote: 45 852 patients admitted to 1250 hospitals within 24 h of suspected acute MI onset were randomly allocated

major_points.text: Intervention dosing was up to 15 mg IV then 200 mg oral daily, with metoprolol compared against matching placebo.
major_points.quote: metoprolol (up to 15 mg intravenous then 200 mg oral daily; n=22 929) or matching placebo (n=22 923).

major_points.text: Co-primary outcomes were (1) composite of death, reinfarction, or cardiac arrest; and (2) death from any cause during scheduled treatment period.
major_points.quote: The two prespecified co-primary outcomes were: (1) composite of death, reinfarction, or cardiac arrest; and (2) death from any cause during the scheduled treatment period.

major_points.text: The co-primary composite outcome was not significantly reduced with metoprolol.
major_points.quote: 2166 (9·4%) patients allocated metoprolol had at least one such event compared with 2261 (9·9%) allocated placebo (odds ratio [OR] 0·96, 95% CI 0·90–1·01; p=0·1).

major_points.text: Metoprolol reduced reinfarction and ventricular fibrillation but increased cardiogenic shock.

absolute_effects.text: Co-primary composite outcome: 2166 (9.4%) vs 2261 (9.9%), absolute difference –4.2 per 1000 (SE 2.8).
Cardiogenic shock: 1141 (5.0%) vs 885 (3.9%), absolute difference 11.2 per 1000 (SE 1.9).

subgroups.text: Prespecified subgroup analyses included age, sex, delay from symptom onset, use of fibrinolytic therapy, Killip class, systolic blood pressure, and heart rate.
subgroups.quote: Others were of those outcomes in certain subgroups (eg, age, sex, delay from symptom onset, use of ﬁbrinolytic therapy, Killip class, systolic blood pressure, heart rate).

subgroups.text: No clearly significant effect on mortality was noted in any patient subcategory considered separately (table 6).
subgroups.quote: Allocation to metoprolol did not produce any clearly signiﬁcant effect on mortality in any of the subcategories of patient considered separately (table 6).

harms.text: Cardiogenic shock occurred more often with metoprolol than placebo.
Persistent hypotension (but no shock) was more frequent with metoprolol than placebo.
Bradycardia was more frequent with metoprolol than placebo.
